changes: scripts/promote-dist.mjs now validates and restores package.json bin targets on the staging tree before evicting the current dist, rejects final symlinks and intermediate-symlink escapes, and preserves the old dist on failure. packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts reports only the compiled runtime version and renders version=unknown when that probe fails. The red and realpath regression suites cover the new safety and diagnostic cases.
usage: Run npm --prefix packages/main run build, then proof-or-stop --version and proof-or-stop doctor. For regression checks run node packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs and node packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs.
expectedOutcome: A dist rebuild leaves packages/main/dist/cli.js executable, proof-or-stop remains runnable, unsafe bin symlink paths cannot chmod files outside staging, and doctor reports the compiled version or version=unknown.
actualTranscript: Focused verification passed: red-global-cli-exec-bit printed GREEN including hermetic c6 for an intermediate-directory symlink escape; global-core-realpath printed ok; packages/main/dist/cli.js was mode 0755.
outcomeDiff: No user-visible difference from the expected outcome.
limitations: Doctor is read-only and reports remediation without changing the host install. On Windows hosts that cannot create symlinks, only the unsupported symlink fixture is explicitly skipped; all other failures remain blocking.
pitfalls: Executable-bit restoration must stay before old-dist eviction. Using post-promotion chmod can replace a working dist before a staging permission failure is discovered; using lexical containment alone can follow intermediate symlinks outside staging.
